transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I’m having a hard time finishing things all the way through at work. Like, I’ll start the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and somehow I’ll leave out the last parts. I know it’s important, and I know my job depends on doing it right, but I keep missing the follow-through.
Did you have trouble finishing schoolwork when you were a child?

Yes. My mom actually still has some of my elementary school report cards, like from around fourth grade, and they say I was bright but needed a lot of reminders to finish classwork and turn in homework. I remember understanding the lessons, but I’d miss parts of the instructions unless the teacher was right there checking on me.
Do you also have this same problem finishing things at home?

Yes, it’s pretty much the same kind of thing. I’ll start something that has steps to it, and I know I need to finish it, but I somehow don’t do the last part. At work it shows up a lot with the sanitation steps, batch logs, or end-of-line paperwork—I’ll get most of it done and then leave off the final pieces, even though I know it really matters.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think of myself as especially restless or fidgety most of the time. I mean, I might shift around like anyone, but it’s not something I’ve really noticed as a big problem.
Have these attention problems caused serious trouble in your relationships?

I’m not sure I’d call it serious trouble. I haven’t really noticed my attention issues causing major relationship problems. Maybe little frustrations here and there, but nothing that stands out as a big pattern to me.
When you’re trying to finish tasks, do you find yourself getting stuck because you’re worrying a lot?
I don’t think it’s usually because I’m worrying a lot. It’s more like I just get off track or have trouble getting the last part done. I’m not sitting there feeling anxious about it most of the time.
Do you get easily distracted when you’re in the middle of a task?

Yes, I do. Even if I start my shift trying to really focus, after a while the cutting, weighing, and checking labels kind of run together. I’ll realize I’ve just been staring at the same tray or the log sheet and not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next.
Besides work, do these same attention problems interfere with things you need to get done in your daily life?
I’m not really sure. I notice it most at work, honestly. Outside of that, I guess I haven’t paid as much attention to whether it’s the same thing, so I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure.
Have these same attention problems ever caused you to miss paying a bill on time?
I’m not sure. I don’t really have a clear example of missing a bill because of it. I’d have to think about that more.
Do these same attention problems make it hard for you to keep your home organized?
I’m not sure. My place isn’t always super organized, but I don’t know if that’s because of the same attention problem or just me not keeping up with it. I haven’t really connected it clearly.
Right now as an adult, do you notice the same trouble finishing multi-step tasks in settings other than work?

I notice it the most at work, honestly. Like I’ll start the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and then somehow the last parts just don’t get done or I leave something out. That’s kind of what brought me in, because even when I know I need to finish it correctly, I still don’t always follow all the way through.
Do you often start tasks but fail to finish them even when you understand what you’re supposed to do?

Yes. That’s actually a big reason I’m here. I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs or the end-of-line paperwork, and I know exactly what I’m supposed to do, but somehow the last parts get missed. It’s frustrating because I know my job depends on finishing them correctly, but I still don’t always follow through all the way.
As an adult, have these attention problems clearly caused you to have trouble in any setting outside of work?
I don’t know that I can clearly say that. I notice it mainly at work. Outside of work, I’m not sure I’ve paid enough attention to connect it the same way.
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve felt depressed most of the day, at least not that I’ve noticed. My main concern has been the focus stuff.
As an adult, have these same focus problems caused you to make mistakes while driving?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed a pattern with driving mistakes, or at least I haven’t connected it to my focus the way I have at work.
As an adult, have these same focus problems clearly caused problems in your home life?
I’m not sure I can clearly say that. At home, I haven’t really noticed specific problems that I’d connect to my focus the same way.
As an adult, have these same focus problems ever clearly caused problems in your finances?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed my focus causing clear financial problems, at least nothing specific I can point to.
Have these same focus problems ever clearly caused you trouble in school or training as an adult?

Yes. With certification modules or training stuff, especially long procedure readings, I put them off until the last possible minute. Sitting there trying to take in all the rules feels almost physically exhausting, so I avoid it, and then it becomes a problem when I’m rushing to get it done.
As an adult, do these same focus problems clearly interfere with chores or other responsibilities at home?
I don’t really know. I haven’t clearly noticed it interfering with chores or responsibilities at home in a specific way.
Did these focus problems get noticeably worse after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

I wouldn’t say it was one specific stressful event. It got noticeably more serious after I switched into full-time meat processing, about two years and four months ago. Since then it’s been a pretty constant problem.
